next_step: Account closed-lost to self-host decision. Re-engage Q4 2026 if infra costs creep or security needs change.
notes:
Account summary: closed-lost — customer formally decided to self-host their inference stack (vLLM + TGI with TensorRT acceleration) citing cost and control.

Timeline / highlights:
- 2025-09-03: inbound interest from ML infra lead (initial qualification). Use-case: high-throughput embed & rerank for financial document search; also chat assistants for traders. Latency target P50 < 100ms on query-heavy routes, throughput ~5k qps for embeddings.
- 2025-10-08: discovery call (AE Maya, SE Carlos). Discussed Redwood hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Customer concerned about token costs at scale and regulatory docs retention.
- 2025-11-12: demo + bench session (Fireflies ff_2025-11-12_orchid-demo). Redwood demoed dedicated pool with autoscale and prefix caching. Customer asked for HSM/KMS integration and audit log retention >5 years.
- 2025-12-05: security review with Orchids' InfoSec (Fireflies ff_2025-12-05_security-review). InfoSec: SOC2 required, HSM for key management, strong egress controls, and local residency for certain datasets. SE provided security FAQ (drive doc).
- 2026-01-18: POC proposal sent (dedicated cluster + canary routing, price estimate). CTO flagged budget freeze; finance requested 6-month runway.
- 2026-02-10: internal reorg at Orchid — champion (Head of ML Ops) left company. Engagement stalled.
- 2026-02-20: final decision call — Orchid to self-host. Reasoning captured below.

Why they self-hosted (customer-quoted reasons):
- "Per-token economics don't pencil out at our scale — running optimized vLLM on our G5/TRT infra is materially cheaper."
- "We need direct control of keys + HSM and complete network isolation; cloud-hosted options add operational uncertainty."
- "We already have an infra team prototyping TGI + vLLM; faster to productize internally than rework procurement."

POC results and technical notes:
- Orchid ran Redwood's sample prompts and compared throughput vs their vLLM bench. vLLM + TensorRT on their HW showed 30-45% lower per-token cost in our workload with acceptable latency for batch embeddings.
- Main gap vs Redwood: they wanted managed autoscaling, rollout tooling, and built-in evals. They plan to adopt open-source toolchain + internal runbooks to cover that.
- Security: their engineering legal required HSM-backed KMS; Redwood's hosted offering could not guarantee customer-managed HSM for the required residency at the time of evaluation. Dedicated offering had long lead times and higher committed cost.

Internal notes (AE/SE):
- Pricing was the decisive factor + loss of champion after reorg. Even with Redwood's dedicated discounts, finance favored capitalizing on existing infra investments.
- We pushed fallbacks: hybrid (private control plane + dedicated GPU), but Org insisted on full on-prem/air-gapped option. They are resourceful and have a strong infra team.
- Action: mark closed-lost, schedule re-engage in Oct 2026. Keep CSM looped for potential lift-and-shift opportunity when they hit scale or need multi-region redundancy.

Next steps (internal):
- Close opportunity in CRM (reason: self-host).
- Upload final security notes to drive (SEC-4412).
- Set reminder: 2026-10-01 to re-open discussion on migration / managed service after 6-9 months of production self-hosting.

Attachments & references: POC cost model (drive doc), demo recording (ff_2025-11-12_orchid-demo), security FAQ and gap analysis (SEC-4412).

Contact quotes:
- CTO: "We'll run vLLM + TRT for now; if ops burden grows, we'll talk to vendors again."
- Head of InfoSec (paraphrase): "Cannot accept keys managed outside our HSM; residency is non-negotiable for these datasets."

Short term risk: high — they may remain on self-host if infra team delivers. Medium term opportunity: possible interest in Redwood Private (on-prem appliance) if we can offer HSM integration + competitive economics.
